plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Streets turn lavender-blue as clouds of trumpet-shaped flowers open on the tree's feathery branches. Fallen blossoms carpet pavements and cars in violet. The display is at its most dramatic when the tree is bare of leaves and covered only in flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late September to November (spring in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of the thousands of these South American trees lining its streets.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree set ablaze with scarlet-orange blossoms. Each flower has one petal streaked with white and yellow. Long dark seed pods hang from the branches after the flowers fade.
plants.bloomingSeason: November to January, at the end of the dry season
plants.funFact: This tree is native to Madagascar but is now planted in tropical regions worldwide, and it is considered threatened in its wild homeland.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub brightens the dim autumn garden with delicate, open flowers that have golden stamens. Many are lightly fragrant. Petals drift down like confetti as the blooms age.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, commonly from October or November through December or January
plants.location: Japan and temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua flowers in autumn, ahead of the better-known Camellia japonica, which blooms in winter and spring.

plants.name: Cyclamen hederifolium
plants.description: Swept-back pink petals rise on slender stems from bare woodland soil. The ivy-shaped leaves, marbled in silver and green, follow the flowers. Patches of them light up shady corners as the days grow short.
plants.bloomingSeason: October to November, into early December
plants.location: Gardens and woodlands of the United Kingdom and Europe, native to southern Europe
plants.funFact: After pollination the flower stalk coils like a spring and pulls the seed capsule down toward the soil. Ants then carry the seeds away.
